written.myAnswer: Isotopes have the same number of electrons and therefore the same electronic arrangement, giving them almost the same chemical properties. Their different numbers of neutrons give them different masses, so some physical properties differ.
A radioactive isotope has an unstable nucleus that emits excess energy as radiation.
For example, ²¹⁰₈₄Po → ²⁰⁶₈₂Pb + ⁴₂He. Polonium-210 decays to stable lead-206.
Tritium has an unstable nucleus, so it emits radiation. The other two hydrogen isotopes are stable.
Radioactive nuclei have an unstable balance of protons and neutrons. They emit radiation as they change towards a more stable state.
Ionizing radiation can transfer enough energy to an atom to remove one or more electrons. The atom then becomes a positively charged ion.

Radioactivity is the emission of radiation from an unstable isotope. Three applications are medical imaging or treatment, carbon-14 dating of organic remains, and detecting flaws in metals or concrete using radiation.
